Standups and Subpoenas
  - POV alternates: Maya then Aaron.
  - Spindle’s Flatiron HQ hums as Sprintboard’s “Smart Minutes” demo wows investors; Maya quietly relies on a shadow calendar-scrape she approved to juice summaries.
  - Apex embeds Aaron in Hudson Yards; his due-diligence checklist flags gaps: DPAs stale, DPIA “in progress,” Snowflake roles unclear. Rishi can’t see product logs; Okta audit is “redacted for velocity.”
  - Tom Reyes, IT admin at a marquee healthcare client, pings with Looker anomalies: “anonymized” meeting-derived tasks echo PHI-ish phrases; existing BAA scope looks insufficient.
  - Aaron traces token scope creep: a service account drifted into the Okta “Eng-Admin” group, granting USAGE on raw.calendar in Snowflake; a legacy S3 bucket with ACL inheritance exposes a limited index of meeting audio hashes.
  - Late-night standup in DUMBO: dry humor over Jira board chaos; chemistry crackles between Maya and Aaron while they triage DPIA sections and draft consent copy. Maya dodges Sloane Mercer’s probing email; Victor pressures for a term-sheet sign by Friday; Leila demands “frictionless” onboarding; Ava’s consent overhaul is sidelined.
  - Jonah “finds” a Looker explore tying “anonymous” attendees to named CRM contacts via calendar crumb joins; he leaks internally that Maya is sandbagging compliance.
  - Cliffhanger: Aaron requests full Okta export; gets a PDF screenshot instead. Badge logs show a 2 a.m. data-center visit tied to Maya’s card. Sloane calls: “Off-book data at Spindle—comment?” Maya’s demo pipeline suddenly goes dark.

The Anonymity Tax
  - POV alternates: Aaron then Maya.
  - Aaron and Maya work from LIC, diffing Snowflake grants; they confirm the vendor ClearLambda is enriching “anonymous” text with third-party corp directories. Elena Volkova stonewalls on sourcing, citing “proprietary blend.”
  - DPIA workshop turns adversarial: Ava pushes high-risk classification; Felix from Apex slacks Aaron: “Bless it by EOD or the round slips.” Victor dangles VP in front of Maya if the term sheet lands.
  - Rishi uncovers that the service account inherited Okta group membership via a mis-tagged SCIM sync; Okta logs are truncated at 30 days—exactly when the scrape spiked. A redacted export smells like someone trimmed scope evidence.
  - Tom Reyes escalates: a Sprintboard-generated task referenced a trauma case Priya handled; Maya realizes healthcare clients slipped in via generic enterprise SKUs without BAAs flagged. Consent is not just thin—it’s off.
  - Date-that’s-also-a-war-room in a DUMBO wine bar: Maya and Aaron trade war stories; sparks turn into a kiss outside as a Slack alert hits—new Looker tiles from Jonah show conversion jumps tied to the shadow feed. He’s queued it for board review.
  - Maya confronts Leila about shipping “Smart Minutes—Zero Click” to beat Sloane’s piece. Leila insists: “We ship; GC can mop.” Aaron catches a midnight edit in the Okta group membership from Maya’s admin token. He confronts her; she denies it and points to badge anomalies being cloneable with visitor temp cards.
  - Sloane’s story drafts with specifics only an insider would know. Tom gives a 48-hour ultimatum: sign a BAA or he pulls licenses and files a complaint. Felix warns Aaron: “If you tank this, you’re off partner track.”
  - Cliffhanger: Looker’s lineage graph reveals that the new “anonymous” model was forked from Maya’s demo workspace—by Jonah. A 72-hour disclosure clock starts as a “security event under evaluation,” colliding with the Series C sign date.

Disclosure Window
  - POV alternates: Maya then Aaron.
  - Maya chooses disclosure over valuation: with Ava, she triggers the incident playbook, freezes ClearLambda ingestion in Snowflake, revokes service tokens in Okta, rotates keys, and archives raw.calendar with legal hold. A blunt internal post admits “unauthorized scope amplification.”
  - Aaron leverages his privacy-engineer past: restores full Okta exports via API, proving a visitor badge cloned Maya’s badge ID; the 2 a.m. edit came from Jonah’s workstation using a shared admin token Leila refused to retire “for velocity.”
  - Boardroom in Hudson Yards: Maya presents a remediation plan—consent-first redesign, explicit opt-in flows, on-device summarization, per-tenant keys, DPAs/BAAs re-papered, Looker explores purged of re-identification joins, and a vendor exit from ClearLambda with clawbacks. She refuses Victor’s ask to “soft-pedal” the healthcare angle.
  - Sloane runs with a tempered scoop: “Spindle hits pause to rebuild consent.” The market doesn’t implode; a smaller, structured round closes with governance terms. Felix backs Aaron’s call, quietly admiring the save.
  - Consequences: Jonah is terminated; Leila is reprimanded and loses change-control authority; Victor cedes a risk committee seat to Ava; Rishi gains log access by charter. Tom signs an interim BAA after seeing the DPIA and a new PHI segregation plan in Snowflake.
  - Relationship choice: on the LIC waterfront, Maya and Aaron negotiate boundaries under scrutiny—no secrets, no shadow data. He won’t join Spindle; instead, he’ll advise pro bono on the privacy backlog until the audit closes. She passes on the immediate VP, choosing to earn it clean. He turns down an Apex promotion tied to “moving fast on gray zones.”
  - Final image: Flatiron standup, quieter and sharper. Jira sprint name: “Friction, On Purpose.” In DUMBO, late-night, they work side-by-side—calendars opt-in only, tokens least-privilege, love with audit logs.
